decisions.reason: The camera is close to the firm's established space optics and supported by in-house R&D, so management can interpret its results and improve it.
The modular navigation camera is close to existing capabilities and has demonstrated flight heritage on ESA's HERA mission, making dropout very unlikely.
The sensor suite builds on the firm's established offer and benefits from the firm's strong R&D and research cooperation, so it is likely to be retained.
Although only mentioned on the website, the miniaturized LiDAR is close to existing optoelectronic know-how and supported by R&D, so management can still learn from it.
The radiation-hard camera is close to the firm's established space camera portfolio and launched recently, so absorptive capacity supports keeping it.
The asteroid navigation camera builds on established imaging capabilities and the firm's R&D base, so management is likely to keep it despite limited website prominence.
